skill.name: decisions
skill.description: Load architectural decision records before choosing an approach, so new work stays consistent with documented rationale.
skill.summary: Review past architectural decisions before making new technical choices.
skill.author: Clouder0

security_audit.summary: All five static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and JSON examples in SKILL.md. The skill only instructs the assistant to inspect local decision records with Read and Glob. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or unsafe command execution was found.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 33 is a Markdown code fence before a Glob example, not Ruby backtick execution. The example uses the allowed Glob tool with a fixed local path.
Line 35 closes the Markdown code fence for the Glob example and does not execute a command. No shell command or user-controlled input is present.
Line 47 starts a fenced JSON example for recording a decision. It is documentation text, not executable shell or Ruby syntax.
Line 49 closes the fenced JSON example and has no command execution behavior. The surrounding content is a static decision-record template.
Line 53 opens another fenced JSON format example. The content describes a local documentation schema and does not invoke external commands.

content.value_statement: Teams often repeat design debates or miss prior rationale. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to review decision records before new choices.
actual_capabilities: Identifies moments when prior architectural decisions should be reviewed.
Points the assistant to decision records under memory/knowledge/decisions/.
Recommends using Glob to list existing decision record files.
Instructs the assistant to read rationale before following or diverging from a decision.
Defines the expected fields for a decision record, including context, options, rationale, and consequences.
limitations: Requires existing decision records in the expected local directory.
Does not validate decision quality or resolve conflicting records by itself.
Does not create files directly; it describes how to record decision knowledge.
Works best when decision records use the documented structure.

use_cases.title: Choose a system architecture
use_cases.description: Review accepted decisions before selecting a framework, storage model, or integration pattern.

use_cases.title: Understand existing patterns
use_cases.description: Find the rationale behind current project conventions before changing implementation direction.

use_cases.title: Document a new tradeoff
use_cases.description: Capture context, options, rationale, and consequences after a significant technical choice.

prompt_templates.title: Check prior decisions
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review before a small technical choice.
prompt_templates.prompt: Before we choose an approach, use the decisions skill to check existing decision records. Summarize any relevant rationale in plain language.

prompt_templates.title: Compare a proposal with history
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of a proposed design change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the decisions skill to review prior decisions related to this proposal. Tell me whether the proposal aligns with them or needs a documented exception.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a decision record
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the decisions skill to help draft a decision record for this choice. Include context, options, the selected decision, rationale, and consequences.

prompt_templates.title: Audit architectural consistency
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review across several planned changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the decisions skill to review all relevant decision records for these planned changes. Identify conflicts, missing rationale, and decisions that need updates.

output_examples.input: Should we replace the current queue system?
output_examples.output: The assistant lists relevant decision records, summarizes the original queue rationale, and notes whether the replacement aligns with accepted constraints.

output_examples.input: Document why we chose PostgreSQL over a document database.
output_examples.output: The assistant produces a decision summary with context, considered options, final choice, rationale, and expected consequences.

output_examples.input: Are our new API plans consistent with past architecture decisions?
output_examples.output: The assistant identifies matching records, calls out conflicts, and recommends whether to follow, revise, or document an exception.

best_practices: Review existing decision records before making a significant technical change.
Record the rationale and consequences, not only the final choice.
Document clear reasons when a new decision diverges from an accepted one.
anti_patterns: Using the skill after implementation, when the decision can no longer guide the work.
Recording choices without context, alternatives, or consequences.
Treating old decisions as permanent when project constraints have changed.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps the assistant review architectural decision records before making or documenting technical choices.

faq.question: Which tools does it use?
faq.answer: It is designed for Read and Glob, so the assistant can find and inspect local decision records.

faq.question: Does it make decisions automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides context from past decisions so users can make informed choices.

faq.question: Where should decision records be stored?
faq.answer: The skill points to memory/knowledge/decisions/ as the expected location for decision records.

faq.question: Can it help write a new decision record?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes the fields to include, such as context, options, rationale, and consequences.

faq.question: Is this skill safe for marketplace use?
faq.answer: The reviewed file only references local reading and listing of decision records. The static command findings were code-fence false positives.
